newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-HENMAN TO PLAY ROSSET IN EC TOURNAMENT FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HENMAN TO PLAY ROSSET IN EC TOURNAMENT FINAL.

text.p: Marc Rosset recovered from a shaky start to beat Czech Petr Korda 7-6 6-3 on Saturday and set up a final with British number one Tim Henman in the European Community championship.
"I like this guy...I like his style," Rosset said of Henman. "He's a smart player." Sunday's final will be their first meeting.
Earlier, sixth-seeded Henman -- the only seed to survive the earlier rounds -- reached his third final of the year when he beat unseeded Marc Goellner 6-4 6-4.
Rosset quickly fell 4-1 behind as Korda's powerful groundstrokes and accurate drop shots gave him the edge.
The former Olympic champion drew a loud cheer when he launched his racket high in the air in frustration and caught it.

"It's my style to always be one break down in the first set because I'm always slow to warm up...but he was returning unbelievably, there was nothing I could do but wait," said Swiss Rosset, who had lost four of his five previous matches against Korda.
But Korda, ranked 33 in the world, faded soon afterwards and was overwhelmed in the tie-break 7-2.
Rosset used his big serve to keep the momentum going in the second set while Korda folded further under the pressure.
The Czech saved the first match point but succumbed to the second when he hit a backhand passing shot wide.

Henman, the world number 19 who won his first professional title in Sydney last month, broke Goellner in the opening game after the German double-faulted twice and then held his serve to seal the first set in 35 minutes.
He broke again in the opening game of the second set after another Goellner double fault.

Goellner, winner of two tournaments on clay in the past four years, made amends with a service break in the next game but Henman broke again in the fifth game and never looked in danger of losing control.
He served out the match with a love game after one hour 10 minutes.
Henman said had been steadily improving throughout the week and had produced some "very good tennis" against Goellner.
"But I still feel that for the final there is room for improvement," he said.
